title: Identification races the trip-ended message on the same trip
description: This suite's own O9 naming (identification-vs-trip-ended race) differs from the design doc's O9 (two concurrent identifications); see src/scenarios/race.ts for the discrepancy note. The identification (claimed atSec 60) and the trip's own IGN_OFF share the same deliverAtSec (150), signalling to the player that both must be dispatched together without waiting for either to settle first; a genuine race, not array-order delivery, is the point (the scenario repeats this fixture 5 times). One HARDBRAKE at atSec 30, before the identification's claimed atSec 60, so the driver is still unknown when it is raised: this is the violation the `allAssignedTo: 'A'` assertion depends on, so proving violation attribution converges on A is not vacuously true against an empty trip (defect H2). Must prove: regardless of which of the two arrives first, exactly one row ends up carrying is_assignee_source (proving the partial unique index, not just application logic, prevents a duplicate claim), and the asset assignee, trip assignee, and violation attribution all converge on A. Must NOT change: no run of the 5 repeats may produce two rows with is_assignee_source true, or an assignee other than A.
